what_it_does: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique where an AI model looks up relevant documents before generating an answer, using a step called nearest-neighbor search to find documents whose meaning most closely matches the query. Approximate versions of that search are fast but sometimes return the wrong documents, degrading answer quality. DReX solves this by doing an exact search — guaranteed correct results — while keeping it fast through a two-stage filter: an early pass runs inside the memory chips themselves (avoiding the costly step of shipping all the data to the main processor), and only the surviving candidates are handed off to a dedicated nearby compute unit for the final exact ranking. This is from the abstract only, so the precise speedup numbers and full design details are not yet confirmed.
